::: {.callout-note}
## How the two days are built
Eight sessions. Each one is **a short lecture → live coding → "your turn"**, and each has its own self-guided
**tutorial** (menu above) that contains everything we typed, the outputs, the exercises and their solutions — so you
can redo the session at home, or catch up if you fall behind in the room.

Four model families carry the workshop: **random forests, support vector machines, XGBoost and neural networks**.
Logistic regression appears only as the baseline you already know. Day 1 builds the pipeline and the first two
families; Day 2 adds the third, teaches you to validate, tune, evaluate and explain, and ends with neural networks.
:::

**Dataset for both days:** `data/nhms_synthetic.csv` — 5,000 simulated Malaysian adults, NHMS-style variables.
**The question for both days:** *who has undiagnosed type 2 diabetes?* (A take-home challenge on undiagnosed
hypertension closes Tutorial 7.)

::: {.callout-tip}
## If you are running late
Every "Your turn" block is self-contained in its tutorial and can be finished at home. Protect the live coding and,
on Day 2, protect the neural-network theory block — it is the content people came for and the hardest to self-teach.
:::

## Learning outcomes

By the end of the two days participants can:

1. Distinguish a predictive from an explanatory model and choose the right validation design for a prediction question.
2. Build a leak-free `tidymodels` pipeline: stratified split, recipe, workflow, resampling.
3. Fit, compare and tune **random forests, support vector machines, gradient-boosted trees and multilayer perceptrons**, and explain in plain language how each one learns.
4. Evaluate a classifier the way a clinician needs it evaluated — sensitivity, specificity and PPV at the real prevalence, ROC and PR curves, calibration, Brier score — and choose a defensible decision threshold.
5. Explain a model globally (importance, partial dependence) and locally (SHAP), and state what those explanations do and do not mean.
6. Describe what a neural network computes, how backpropagation trains it, and when it is the wrong tool.
7. Report a model in line with TRIPOD+AI.
